functionDeclarations.name: list_brands
functionDeclarations.description: The brand catalogue. There is no name search — page through it (there are rarely more than a hundred) and match the brand name to get the id the products index filters by. (GET /api/v2/brands)

functionDeclarations.name: list_products_by_brand
functionDeclarations.description: Paginated products. Filter by brand ID to scope an enrichment run to one supplier's catalogue; parent_id and type tell you which rows are matrix children. (GET /api/v2/products)

filter[brand_id].description: Brand id from list-brands. Comma-separate several ids, e.g. "16,22".

filter[search].description: Free-text search over SKU / name / barcode / MPN / brand.

functionDeclarations.name: get_product
functionDeclarations.description: One product in full — name, sku, brand, image / image_url / other_images, parent_id, type, matrix_product, variations, attributes, default_supplier. The image is what the review report shows so the reviewer knows what they are approving. (GET /api/v2/products/{product})

functionDeclarations.name: get_product_listings
functionDeclarations.description: The product's live listings across every channel — one row per listing with integration_name, channel_name, listing_url and title. It does NOT carry the ids needed to fetch the channel's own copy; take each row's id to get-product-listing for those. (GET /api/v2/products/{product}/listings)

functionDeclarations.name: get_product_listing
functionDeclarations.description: One listing in full. integration_instance_id and document_id (the channel-product id) are what the Amazon / eBay channel-product endpoints below take. (GET /api/v2/product-listings/{productListing})

productListing.description: The product listing id (a row id from get-product-listings).

functionDeclarations.name: get_amazon_channel_product
functionDeclarations.description: An Amazon channel product with its catalog data. Ask for catalog_data explicitly — it carries attributes.product_description[].value, attributes.bullet_point[].value and attributes.item_name[].value, the copy Amazon actually shows. (GET /api/amazon/{integrationInstance}/products/{product})

integrationInstance.description: The Amazon integration instance id (integration_instance_id on the listing row).

product.description: The Amazon channel-product id (document_id on the listing row).

included.description: JSON array of extra fields to include. Pass ["catalog_data"].

functionDeclarations.name: get_ebay_channel_product_raw
functionDeclarations.description: The live eBay item straight from eBay (GetItem), including its Description HTML — the stored channel product does not carry it, so this is the only way to read eBay copy. (GET /api/ebay/{integrationInstance}/products/{product}/raw)

product.description: The eBay channel-product id (document_id on the listing row).

functionDeclarations.name: get_product_attributes
functionDeclarations.description: The product's attribute values — direct rows plus attribute-group rows — including any description already written for another channel (amazon_description, ebay_description) and the target channel attribute if it has been filled before. Use this, not the un-grouped /attributes, which does not carry values. (GET /api/products/{productId}/attributes-grouped)

functionDeclarations.name: list_attributes
functionDeclarations.description: The attribute catalogue — check whether the channel's description attribute exists before creating it. (GET /api/v2/attributes)

functionDeclarations.name: create_attribute
functionDeclarations.description: Create the channel-specific description attribute. Use type longtext; set display_options.is_html when the channel renders HTML so the PIM opens a rich-text editor. (POST /api/attributes)

name.description: Follow the existing convention {channel}_description, e.g. tiktokshop_description.

display_options.description: {"is_html": true} when the channel renders HTML (TikTok Shop, eBay, Shopify); omit for plain-text channels (Amazon, Walmart).

notes.description: Where the value is used, e.g. "Mapped to TikTok Shop → Description on the channel profile."

functionDeclarations.name: generate_listing_content
functionDeclarations.description: Ask SKU.io's AI for channel-correct content. Pass everything you gathered as source_material; the model amalgamates it under the target channel's own description rules (format, length, structure) and returns a rationale explaining what it used. Returned for review only — nothing is written. (POST /api/ai/listing-content)

sales_channel_id.description: The TARGET sales channel — the one the description is for.

fields.description: Which pieces to generate: ["description"], ["title"], or both. The title follows the channel's own cap and shape (brand first, keyword-rich).

source_material.description: Up to 10 entries of {label, text} — existing copy from other channels, the manufacturer's page, a supplier sheet. Label each with its origin so the rationale can name it. Each text up to 8000 characters.

description_format.description: "html" or "plain". Omit to use the channel's own rule (TikTok Shop html, Amazon plain, ...).

description_max_length.description: Override the channel's length cap (100-20000). Omit to use the channel's own.

include_product_attributes.description: Feed the product's own attributes as facts (default true).

target_keywords.description: Up to 25 keywords to weave in where truthful.

functionDeclarations.name: set_product_attributes
functionDeclarations.description: Write attribute values on a product. Only ever call this with descriptions the reviewer approved. Send the attribute by name; other attributes are left untouched. (PUT /api/products/{productId}/attributes)

functionDeclarations.name: get_supplier
functionDeclarations.description: The supplier record — email, purchase_order_email, primary_contact_name, website. Used to address the enrichment request when no copy exists anywhere. (GET /api/v2/suppliers/{supplier})

supplier.description: The supplier id (default_supplier.id on the product).

functionDeclarations.name: sync_listing_profile_mappings
functionDeclarations.description: Point the channel profile's Description at the new attribute so every listing on that channel reads it. Full replace — send the profile's complete mapping set. (PUT /api/v2/sales-channels/{salesChannel}/listing-profiles/{profile}/mappings)

mappings.description: Complete set of {channel_field_name, source_type, source_value}. For the description: {"channel_field_name":"Description","source_type":"product_attribute","source_value":"<attribute id>"}
